question.:question/problem:
$$
f(t,z)=⟨3\sec  t,\,\text{_____},\,z⟩,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})
$$

The vector-valued function $f(t,z)$ above parametrizes one sheet of the hyperbolic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as ${x}^{2}-{y}^{2}=9$ for $x\ge 3.$ What is the second component of $f?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the hyperbola ${x}^{2}-{y}^{2}=9$ for $x\ge 3$ in $xy$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨x,y⟩=⟨3\sec  t,\,3\tan  t⟩,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})
$$

since 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-{y}^{2} & =(3\sec  t)^{2}-(3\tan  t)^{2} \\  & =9(\sec^{2} t-\tan^{2} t) \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t,z) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨3\sec  t,\,3\tan  t,\,z⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})$ and $z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the second component of $f$ is $3\tan  t.$

The vector-valued function $f(y, t)$ above parametrizes one sheet of the hyperbolic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $6z^{2} - 9x^{2} = 54$ for $z \ge 3$. What is the first component of $f$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the hyperbola $\frac{z^2}{9}-\frac{x^2}{6}=1$ for $z\ge 3$ in $xz$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨x,\,z⟩=⟨\sqrt{6}\tan t,\,3\sec t⟩,\quad t\in(-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2})
$$

since 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{z^2}{9}-\frac{x^2}{6}&=\frac{(3\sec t)^2}{9}-\frac{(\sqrt{6}\tan t)^2}{6}\\&=\frac{9\sec^2 t}{9}-\frac{6\tan^2 t}{6}\\&=\sec^2 t-\tan^2 t\\&=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y,t)&=⟨x,\,y,\,z⟩\\&=⟨\sqrt{6}\tan t,\,y,\,3\sec t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in(-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2})$ and $y\in(-\infty,\infty).$

Therefore, the first component of $f$ is $\sqrt{6}\tan t.$

f(y,t)=⟨1\tan  t,\,y,\,\text{_____}⟩,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})
$$

The vector-valued function $f(y,t)$ above parametrizes one sheet of the hyperbolic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as ${z}^{2}-{x}^{2}=1$ for $z\ge 1.$ What is the third component of $f?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the hyperbola ${z}^{2}-{x}^{2}=1$ for $z\ge 1$ in $xz$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨x,\,z⟩=⟨1\tan  t,\,1\sec  t⟩,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})
$$

since 

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{2}-{x}^{2} & =(1\sec  t)^{2}-(1\tan  t)^{2} \\  & =1\sec^{2} t-1\tan^{2} t \\  & =1(\sec^{2} t-\tan^{2} t) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y,t) & =⟨x,\,y,\,z⟩ \\  & =⟨1\tan  t,\,y,\,1\sec  t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2})$ and $y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the third component of $f$ is $1\sec  t.$
